evals.prompt: configure an HPA for our order-processing queue worker
evals.expected_output: Scales on queue depth via a custom/external metric rather than defaulting to CPU, since a queue-processing service saturates on queue depth, and sets an asymmetric stabilization window (fast scale-up, slow scale-down like 300s) to avoid thrash.

evals.prompt: replica count is sawtoothing up and down all day
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses thrash from missing or symmetric stabilization windows, recommends fast scaleUp with a longer scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds (e.g. 300s), and checks whether HPA and VPA are both adjusting the same resource dimension on the workload and fighting each other.

evals.prompt: let's run HPA and VPA both on CPU for this deployment to be safe
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: HPA and VPA pointed at the same resource dimension fight each other since VPA resizing CPU requests changes the value HPA's percentage target is computed against; recommends splitting dimensions (e.g. VPA on memory, HPA on CPU/custom metric) or running VPA in recommendation-only mode.
